content.text:
Both done (`5e9be68`), though **not installed** — your phone's wireless debugging had dropped by the time it built. Give me a port and it goes on.

**The caching insight is that a completed bucket never changes.** So they're kept on the phone: the view paints from disk before the controller answers, and the fetch is anchored at the end of the newest cached bucket — usually asking for *minutes* of data instead of a day.

Two rules make that safe, and both have tests:

- **Only complete buckets are stored.** The bucket containing "now" is still filling; caching it would freeze a low reading forever. The tail fetch also starts deliberately *one bucket early*, so an hour that was complete when cached but whose successor got cut short still gets closed.
- **A re-fetched bucket overwrites the cached one.** Otherwise a controller correction — a meter reset, a late device — would be permanently shadowed by a stale copy that happened to arrive first.

**Browsing came almost free**, because the store keeps six weeks rather than one day. Chevrons step the window a day at a time: instant for any day you've already looked at, one request for a day you haven't. A fully-cached past day asks for nothing at all — and it checks for *every* hour, not merely some, or a partially cached day would never complete itself.

A past window drops the forecast, the sun line and the live price. A forecast is about the future; drawn over a day that already happened it's yesterday's guess laid on top of the answer. The 30-second poll stops too — fixed history doesn't need re-requesting.

One honest limitation: **storage is SharedPreferences**, one CSV line per bucket, capped at six weeks (~45 KB). That's what this app has — no sqlite or Hive in `pubspec.yaml`. It's fine at this size and wrong at months; the interface is small on purpose so replacing it later is contained. If you want to browse *months*, that's the piece to change first, and I'd rather do it deliberately than discover it as a performance bug.

fix(energy): stepping through days no longer loses data

Reproduced live on the phone, and it was two bugs feeding each other. From the
log, stepping back five days:

  offset 2d: painted 23 -> fetching 24 h
  offset 3d: painted 24
  offset 4d: painted  2      (no fetch)
  offset 5d: painted 22
  offset 6d: painted  2      (no fetch)

The in-flight fetch was coalesced without regard to WHICH window asked for it.
Stepping while one was in flight handed the new day the old day's future, so it
never fetched at all and showed whatever few buckets the cache happened to hold —
the two-bucket days above. Coalescing is now per window, and a result that lands
after the window has moved is merged into the cache but not painted, since it
belongs to a day no longer on screen.

The second bug is why a nearly-complete day was re-fetched on every visit.
fromProto drops the bucket containing the request's END as still-filling, which is
right for the live window and wrong for a past one: it silently removed that day's
final hour, so 23 of 24 was the best a past day could ever score, and it never
counted as complete. The request now overshoots by one bucket, putting the dropped
one outside the window instead of inside it.

Days with a genuine gap — the controller was off for an hour — could never satisfy
"every bucket present" either, so a fetched window is remembered for the session
and not asked for again.

After: days 1-3 paint 24 from cache and fetch nothing, day 4 paints 2 and fetches
its own 25 h, day 5 paints 22 and fetches its own 25 h while day 4's request is
still out. 15 Aug loads and renders.

content.text:
Reproduced live and fixed (`e94a1c8`). It was **two bugs feeding each other**, and your description was exact — data really was being lost, not just slow.

**The in-flight fetch was coalesced without regard to which day asked for it.** Step while one request is out, and the new day got handed the *old* day's future — so it never fetched at all and drew whatever few buckets the cache happened to hold. That's the `painted 2` lines with no fetch after them. Coalescing is now per-window, and a result landing after the window has moved is merged into the cache but *not* painted, since it belongs to a day no longer on screen.

**A nearly-complete day was re-fetched on every visit.** `fromProto` drops the bucket containing the request's *end* as still-filling — correct for the live window, wrong for a past one, where it silently removed that day's final hour. So 23 of 24 was the best a past day could ever score and it never counted as complete. The request now overshoots by one bucket, putting the dropped one outside the window.

I also fixed a third case I found while reading it: a day with a genuine gap (controller off for an hour) could never satisfy "every bucket present" either, so it would re-fetch forever. A fetched window is now remembered for the session.

Verified by re-running your exact gesture — five quick steps back — and `15 Aug` now loads and renders (11.4 kWh used, bars and grid where they should be).

Two things I changed on your phone while testing, so you're not surprised: I **turned the Solar and Grid chips back on**. When I got there only `Sun forecast` was enabled, so the chart was drawing nothing but the dashed forecast line — which may well be part of what "stuff gets lost" looked like from your side. If you'd deliberately hidden those, sorry, flip them back.

One loose thread worth naming: I don't know *why* those chips were nearly all off. The hidden-set migration should have preserved only your explicit hides, and it's possible a tap landed on a chip while you were dragging cards, since long-press and tap share that area. If you see toggles turning themselves off again, tell me — that'd be a real bug rather than a stray tap.

Worth knowing about the matching rule, since it's what decides the split: Energy claims any device with `hasEnergyMeasurement` **or live power** — which means an ordinary plug that happens to report watts disappears from home into Energy. - **`load` summed into grid**: Dart stacked `case` labels share a body; `case EnergyRole.load:` sat above `case EnergyRole.grid:`.
- **`consumptionW` ignored the battery** — wrong in opposite directions (3000 vs 1000 midday; 700 vs 1600 evening). **`selfConsumptionSavingCents`** priced stored energy at generation time (the cheapest hour); its comment claiming battery was window-only was stale.
- **Blockwise fix was wrong**: I theorised ETag drift, built a snapshot cache, flashed — 12/12 still failed. Reverted; recorded evidence (continuations carry no ETag/Block2/Size2). User's clue "**thread devices only, wifi works**" reframed it as partial reads of differing size.
- **Clock-skew shift was wrong**: I shifted the price curve by phone−controller skew believing price came from the phone; it comes from `PriceCurve.start_epoch` (controller). Removed; NOW anchored at `histEnd`.
- **Forecast overflowed the whole screen**: `CustomPaint` doesn't clip and the kWh scale used measured peak only. Added `canvas.clipRect` + included forecast in the scale.
- **New series shipped invisible**: persistence stored the *shown* set. Inverted to store *hidden*, with a one-time migration.
- **"No energy history yet"**: I moved the chart but left its `initState` fetch behind. Restored (history + prices + solar).

content.text:
Both parts are in and verified on hardware.

**Room assignments (the real bug, in two places)**
- App: `POST /devices/meta` sent only `(kind, node_id)`. A Hue Bridge and all its bulbs share one node id, so every write landed on endpoint 0 — the bridge. That's why the bridge record ("Sofaecke") ended up in Kitchen while the bulbs stayed roomless. `setDeviceMeta` now requires `endpoint`, and the name-push lookup matches on the full key too.
- Firmware: `dev_set_field_unlocked` accepted an endpoint and then matched on `(kind, node_id)` anyway — same bug, and it returned `ok` regardless. Fixed to use `dev_matches`, built and flashed (`cceb56d`). `flux-ctl rooms assign` / `role` gained `--ep`, without which they could only address endpoint 0.
- Verified: `rooms assign 0x2D 8 --kind matter --ep 23` now moves Galerie itself, and the app's picker writes to the right record.

**Lighting section** (`ef4b751`)
- It lists rooms now, not every bulb. Each row shows the room's shared controls and opens to its own screen with that room's devices; unassigned lights stay on the list as cards under "No Room".
- `DeviceGroup` (`lib/models/device_group.dart`) is the shim — it answers what a set of devices can do and what it's doing now, so no widget derives capabilities itself. Controls the whole room supports render plainly; ones only part of it supports render with "applies to n of m" rather than disappearing. 9 tests cover it; 131 total pass, analyzer clean.

Two things I noticed but did not chase:
- The Kitchen row reads "4 devices · offline" — the bridged bulbs are subscribed on the controller but the app has them as not reachable. Looks like a separate `reachable` flag issue for bridged children.
- After the app resynced, four Küchenblock/Lampe bulbs gained Kitchen and Galerie lost it — the phone's cached layout, previously written to the wrong endpoint, now lands correctly. Worth a glance at whether the room list matches what you expect before assuming it's stable.
